title: Technical Debt Artefact (v1.1.0)
description: A technical debt item: a shortfall in the architecture or its build, taken on deliberately or found later, that costs something to carry (the interest) and something to put right (the principal). It is a consequence of a decision, recorded among that decision's consequences, and once settled is attached to the decision that repaid it, so the debt is never separated from the reasoning that made it acceptable. Fowler's quadrant classifies how it was taken on.

debt_status.description: open: carried, with no plan to repay yet. scheduled: a repayment is planned. repaid: put right, by the decision in repaid_by. written-off: accepted for good, or gone with what carried it.

quadrant.description: How the debt was taken on (Fowler's technical debt quadrant).

principal.description: What it would take to put right.

interest.description: What carrying it costs, and how that grows.

repayment.description: The plan to repay it, when there is one.

consequence_of.description: The decision the debt is a consequence of: the one that took it on, or, for debt found rather than chosen, the one that accepted it. The inverse of consequences.technical_debt on the decision record.

repaid_by.description: The decision that repays the debt. The inverse of repays_debt on the decision record.

affects.description: The artefacts that carry the debt: capabilities, building blocks, patterns, services, stores or nodes.

allOf.$comment: A repaid debt names the decision that repaid it.
